title: Should I call her?
goal: Use the plain conditional -sA to imagine, to wonder what to do, and to give advice: param olsa, gitsem mi, gitsen iyi olur.

intro.text: `-sA` straight on the stem imagines (*Param olsa alırım*, If I had the money, I'd buy it) or wonders (*Gitsem mi?*, Should I go?). With *iyi olur* it gives advice: *Doktora gitsen iyi olur* (You'd better see a doctor).

vocab.en: lottery (piyango çıkmak: to win the lottery)

exercises.label: *gitmek* + `-sA`: if I went, if you went…
exercises.explain: `-sA` starts with a consonant, so *git-* keeps its t: *gitsem*, never *gidsem*. The endings are those of the past: *gitsem* like *gittim*.
The negative `-mA` goes before `-sA`, both with a after *yap-*; **we** is *-k*, as in *yaptık*: *yap-ma-sa-k*.

exercises.question: *Gitsem mi?* What does it mean?

why.2: **If I go** is *gidersem*, and it isn't a question.

exercises.explain: `-sA` + *mi* wonders what to do: *Git-se-m mi?*, **should I go?**

exercises.en: You'd better go to the doctor.

reject.why: *Gitmelisin* (you must go) is correct Turkish, but *iyi olur* needs `-sA`: *gitsen iyi olur*.

exercises.explain: `-sA` + *iyi olur* is friendly advice: *gitsen iyi olur*, or *gitseniz* to someone you call *siz*.

exercises.en: If I had the money, I'd buy this car.

accept: What would you do if you won the lottery?
If you won the lottery, what would you do?
What would you do if you [win|were to win] the lottery?
If you [win|were to win] the lottery, what would you do?

exercises.prompt: Is it all right if I sit here?

exercises.question: Your friend has a bad cold. Which sentence is friendly advice?
exercises.explain: *dinlen-se-n iyi olur*: **you'd better rest a bit**.

exercises.en: Shall we go to the cinema tonight?

exercises.prompt: I wonder if I should call her.

reject.why: *Ararsam* is a real **if**, and it can't take *mi*. To wonder **should I call?**, use plain `-sA`: *arasam mı?*

exercises.text: Hava çok güzel, bugün denize ___ iyi olur.
exercises.en: The weather's lovely; it would be nice to go to the sea today.
exercises.explain: `-sA` + *iyi olur*: *gitsek iyi olur*, **it would be good if we went**. *Gidersek* needs a main clause of its own, and *gidelim* stands alone.

accept: Come early tomorrow if [you can|it is possible].
If [you can|it is possible], come early tomorrow.
Please come early tomorrow if [possible|you can|it is possible].
If [possible|you can|it is possible], please come early tomorrow.
